feedback: Written before this robot has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. (1) Iteration 3 (entityR2B) showed that widening the array to +/-0.04 m at 20 mm spacing, with kp raised from 2.0 to 3.0, reduced every track. The oval fell from 20/20 finishes (iteration 1) to 0/20 at progress 0.43. Because the array and the kp change were altered together, the cause is not isolated. The 20 mm gaps and the higher gain are both plausible, so I have restored the iteration 1 array and kept kp at 2.0. (2) Iteration 1 (entityR2B) is the best measured design: oval 20/20 at max_error 0.025 m, s-bend 8/20, slalom 0/20 at progress 0.18 with about 2 line-loss events. The slalom and s-bend failures are drift off the tape, not jitter (steering_oscillation 0.23 to 0.31), so the question is how much turn authority the robot has at the bends. (3) Body_width has no effect on the off-track limit at 0.12 m (the 0.06 m floor governs), so it is not a lever. Change rules for the next race: if slalom progress rises above 0.18 and the oval still finishes, keep wheel_track at 0.10 m and try 0.09 m to add more turn authority. If the oval's steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4 or the oval finish rate drops, return to wheel_track 0.12 m and try mass 0.45 kg, which should reduce the wheel-speed demand without changing turn gain. If slalom or s-bend still shows line_loss_events of 1 or more at a similar progress, the lever is not turn authority alone, and the next step is sensor y = 0.065 m to give earlier sight of the bends.
requested_changes: Try wheel_track 0.10 m (as in this package). If slalom progress rises above 0.18 while the oval still finishes 20 of 20, try 0.09 m next, since iteration 1 showed the slalom failing from drift with turn authority as the constraint.

If the oval's steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4 or the oval finish rate drops below 1.0, return to wheel_track 0.12 m and try mass 0.45 kg. Iteration 1 (oval steering_oscillation 0.25) and iteration 3 (oval failure at 0.43 progress) show that the controller is sensitive to gain changes, so reducing wheel demand is safer than adding gain.

If slalom or s-bend still shows line_loss_events of 1 or more at a similar progress, try sensor y = 0.065 m with the iteration 1 array, since the sharp bends may need earlier sight. Keep sensor x at +/-0.024 m, because iteration 3 showed that the wider 20 mm array degraded performance.
